dedupe_keys.name: culebra puerto rico hybrid microgrid feasibility study for critical facilities epa and nrel

description: This EPA news release, in an archived snapshot, reports the results of a feasibility study of hybrid microgrids for the Puerto Rican island of Culebra, prepared with the National Renewable Energy Laboratory after the 2017 hurricanes. NREL made the initial assessment in April 2018 and presented the results to the mayor in November 2018. The study found that microgrids combining solar photovoltaics, battery storage and diesel generators are potentially economically viable and could improve energy resilience at five critical buildings: a health clinic, police station, fire station, municipal building and wastewater treatment plant, on an island of about 1,800 residents. The University of Puerto Rico at Mayaguez, the Economic Development Administration and the Community Foundation for Puerto Rico took part, the administration announced a 4.1 million dollar grant in June 2019, and NREL published the full study. The release is free to read and states no licence. The report is available online as a document. Caveats: the release summarises the study without cost figures or load data. For simulation, it is a documented investment appraisal for capacity planning and resilience of island critical facilities.
